closing: That was an amazing Math Puzzle Adventure! You cracked fractions, patterns, and speedy puzzles. Give yourselves a round of applause. See you next lesson!

flow.title: What is a fraction?
flow.body: A fraction shows a part of a whole. The TOP number (numerator) tells how many parts we have. The BOTTOM number (denominator) tells how many equal parts the whole is split into. Example: 3/4 of a pizza means the pizza was cut into 4 equal slices and we have 3 of them.
flow.speak: A fraction shows a part of a whole. The top number is the numerator, how many parts we have. The bottom number is the denominator, how many equal parts in total. Like 3 out of 4 pizza slices!

flow.title: Equivalent fractions
flow.body: Two fractions are EQUIVALENT when they show the same amount. Multiply or divide the top and bottom by the same number: 1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8. It's the same slice of pizza, just cut differently!
flow.speak: Equivalent fractions show the same amount. One half equals two quarters equals four eighths. Same pizza, different cuts!

flow.title: Number patterns
flow.body: A pattern follows a rule. Look at 2, 4, 8, 16... each number DOUBLES! Finding the rule is like being a math detective. Always check: add? subtract? multiply?
flow.speak: Number patterns follow a secret rule. Two, four, eight, sixteen. Each number doubles! Be a math detective and find the rule.

questions.text: A chocolate bar has 8 equal pieces. You eat 3. What fraction did you eat?
questions.explanation: You ate 3 pieces out of 8 equal pieces, so the fraction is 3/8.
3/6 simplifies to 1/2 because 3 is half of 6.

questions.text: What comes next in the pattern: 2, 4, 8, 16, ...?
Puzzle: I am a number. Double me, add 4, and you get 20. Who am I?

questions.explanation: These are odd numbers, so 9 comes next.

knowledge_base.a: A fraction shows a part of a whole. The top number (numerator) counts the parts you have, and the bottom number (denominator) shows how many equal parts the whole is divided into.
The numerator is the TOP number of a fraction. It tells how many parts we have. In 3/8, the numerator is 3.
The denominator is the BOTTOM number of a fraction. It tells how many equal parts the whole is split into. In 3/8, the denominator is 8.
Equivalent fractions look different but show the same amount, like 1/2, 2/4 and 4/8. Multiply or divide the top and bottom by the same number to find them.

knowledge_base.q: How do I compare two fractions?
knowledge_base.a: Give both fractions the same denominator, then compare the top numbers. For example 2/3 = 10/15 and 3/5 = 9/15, so 2/3 is bigger.

knowledge_base.q: How do I add fractions with the same denominator?
knowledge_base.a: If the denominators are the same, just add the numerators and keep the denominator: 1/4 + 2/4 = 3/4.

knowledge_base.q: How do I simplify a fraction?
knowledge_base.a: Divide the top and bottom by the same number until you cannot anymore. For example 4/8 divided by 4 becomes 1/2.
A number pattern is a list of numbers that follows a rule, like doubling (2, 4, 8, 16) or adding 2 (1, 3, 5, 7). Find the rule to predict the next number.

knowledge_base.q: What is half of a number?
knowledge_base.a: Half means dividing by 2, or multiplying by 1/2. Half of 10 is 5.

knowledge_base.q: How do I solve a work-backwards puzzle?
knowledge_base.a: Undo each step in reverse order. If double me plus 4 gives 20: subtract 4 to get 16, then halve it to get 8.
